html:
Kazatomprom is the national uranium company of Kazakhstan, founded in 1997. It is the world's largest producer of natural uranium, supplying over 40 percent of the world's new uranium in 2019.

Kazakhstan has some of the largest uranium reserves on earth, much of it in sandy layers deep under the southern steppe. Kazatomprom mostly uses in situ leaching: it pumps a weak acid down wells into the ore, then pumps the uranium-rich liquid back up. This is cheaper than digging mines and needs few workers.

Production grew fast in the 2000s, and around 2009 Kazakhstan passed Canada and Australia as the top producer. The uranium fuels nuclear power stations around the world, many in China, Europe and Russia. In 2018 the state sold part of the company on the London stock exchange and the Astana International Financial Centre. It is an irony of history that a country scarred by the Semipalatinsk nuclear tests became the world's main uranium supplier.
sum: Kazatomprom is the national uranium company of Kazakhstan, founded in 1997. It is the world's largest producer of natural uranium, supplying over 40 percent of the world's new uranium in 2019.
